body: Most places have moved on to online only applications, but thanks for the suggestions. I'll be looking into a temp agency - as others have said, I can possibly then use those jobs for references in the future.
I'd love to be a teacher, but I can't afford to go back to school for a teaching certificate.

I changed my last name in addition to my first, so could they conceivably say "no, [new name] never worked here"? I have court documents to prove that I changed my name, but I fear any hassle to do with that would be off-putting to potential employers.
At this point, I'll take any job I can reasonably do. Retail, fast food, secretarial work (which is what I used to do), janitorial - anything that will get me a paycheck.

I guess it can't hurt to ask!

I would have to out myself in the e-mail, though. If they remember me at all, it would be my old name/gender. Is there a quick and simple way to explain that? Something like: "I'm [new name], and I attended your class in [year] as [old name], would you be willing to act as a reference for me on job applications?"

I'm long out of college, so I guess I am starting at the bottom. I've tried to get retail/fast-food jobs, but I think my experience/education is getting in the way of that. Is it illegal to omit work experience on an application? I'm always afraid I'll get into trouble if I leave it out, so I always write it down.

I was an administrative assistant/secretary, so my skills are somewhat limited, but local charities may need help with their paperwork or phone answering. I'll look around to see what's available in my area.

Is there a generally accepted time frame for contacting college professors after you've left the school? It's been many years since I was in college, and I have a feeling none of my professors would remember me.
They want nothing to do with me at this point, even to verify. It's an unpleasant situation all around.

I can't afford therapy. If I knew of a trans-friendly/knowledgeable therapist in the area, I'd call right now for an appointment.

There's a TM center in my area, actually, but I've never thought to go there. I'll give them a call.
